title: Quiet Shift: Canine Comfort Drill
premise: A playful stealth-timing arcade game where you calm a dog by petting it only when patrolling guards are not looking.
interaction_model: Single-screen hold-and-release interaction on touch, mouse, or spacebar, with menu-driven cosmetic, sandbox, chat, and cheat side systems.
objective: Fill the calm meter to 100% without petting while any guard is fully facing forward.
progression: Rounds advance by level, increasing patrol count and pace; wins grant coins based on difficulty, which unlock cosmetic dog skins, while sandbox mode allows custom guard layout testing.
theme: Arcade stealth comedy with canine care, patrol surveillance, and toy-like police/drill framing.
mood: Cute, tense, mischievous, lighthearted, and slightly absurd.
likely_audience: Casual web players, kids-to-teens, and players who enjoy simple reaction games, pet themes, and customizable cosmetics.
confidence_notes: High confidence that the core game is a stealth-timing petting loop driven by guard patrol states.
High confidence that cosmetics, sandbox editing, and chat are secondary meta features rather than the primary objective.
Medium confidence on thematic labeling because the game presents police/guard imagery in a cartoon, abstract, non-simulation context.
recreation_prompt: Recreate a browser-based single-screen arcade stealth game called "Quiet Shift: Canine Comfort Drill" where the player calms a cute dog by holding down on the screen, clicking, touching, or pressing space to pet it, but must instantly stop whenever patrolling guards turn to look forward. Present the game as a bright, playful cartoon scene with a dog on one side of a grassy field, several guard characters across the scene, a large calm meter at the top, a level display, coin count, and animated warning/success feedback. Build the main loop around guards cycling through clear states: safe while facing away, a short warning tell, then a looking state with a visible flashlight or detection cone. While the player is petting during safe windows, the calm meter rises, the dog looks happier, hearts appear, and affectionate feedback can pop in; if the player keeps petting while a guard is fully looking, the run fails and a spotted result screen appears. Winning a round should happen when the calm meter reaches 100%, triggering celebratory effects, coin rewards based on selected difficulty, and automatic progression to the next level with more or faster guards. Include three difficulty modes that change patrol speed and rewards. Add a start menu hub with buttons for starting the drill, opening a cosmetic shop, toggling cheats, chatting with a simple patrol operator, entering a sandbox guard-placement editor, and opening a creator screen where players can draw or upload custom art for the dog and the guards. Save coins, unlocks, equipped skin, custom images, and sandbox layouts locally. Keep the overall tone cute, tense, and slightly mischievous, with glassy arcade UI panels, upbeat audio cues, and a clean mobile-friendly touch layout.
